scope: Six prior test functions flipped from the OME-1220 rule to the OME-1687 rule (a retry never makes a call, an operation or a saving unpriced): test_a_miss_retried_after_a_possibly_billed_failure_is_unpriced, test_a_possibly_billed_retry_is_unpriced_in_the_retained_operation, test_a_hit_after_a_retry_reports_an_unknown_price_not_a_zero_one, test_a_retried_miss_is_unpriced_too, test_a_hit_after_a_transport_retry_is_not_priced, test_a_withdrawn_price_lands_in_the_unpriced_bucket_and_no_total (each renamed to state the new rule), the test_ambiguous_retry_pricing module docstring, and one comment-only edit in test_signal_accounting.py::test_a_retried_hit_still_gives_the_reference_numbers. No other prior test changes. Second approval (user, 2026-10-20, decision B): prose only, no test logic — the module docstring of test_cache_hit_retry_pricing.py; in test_cache_saved_cost.py the section header above test_a_hit_after_a_transport_retry_claims_its_saving and the docstring of test_a_hit_with_no_retry_is_still_priced; in test_ambiguous_retry_pricing.py the rename of test_an_unpriced_retried_miss_keeps_its_token_counts to test_a_retried_miss_keeps_its_token_counts and its comment (assertions unchanged).
reason: User decision 2026-10-20 (OME-1687, cost of intelligence): the leaderboard shows the price of a model's successful requests in a perfect world where every model answers on the first attempt, so a retry is an infrastructure event and must not make a price unknown. This reverses OME-1220 D1. The retry flag stays as a recorded fact (D4) and its prior tests stay unchanged.
